item.title: Hear a debate about conserving a changing mural
item.summary: A conservator and organiser weigh authenticity when a wall painting has multiple states.
item.transcript_text:
Organiser: The artist has sent an opening-day photo and asked us to repaint to match.
Conservator: The photo is useful, but it selects one day in a long public life. The artist invited residents to add marks in the second season. Some now sit under another coat.
Organiser: Then do we keep the latest version because it's newest?
Conservator: Newness isn't the test. Imagine removing a layer as damage, then finding out it was part of the project. Record what's there, check which additions were invited, and decide with the artist and community how much change is justified. A digital reconstruction could show the first version without sacrificing the current one.
Organiser: So the photo illustrates one state. It doesn't direct us to remove the others.

questions.prompt: What is inadequate about using only the photo to restore the wall?
options: It shows an unrelated wall
It was taken after the additions appeared
It privileges a moment over changes that may belong to the work
It does not show any original colours
questions.explanation: A single moment does not settle the status of later intentional changes.

options: They prove the newest coat is the only authentic one
They make the boundary between part of the work and later damage less clear
They establish that the photo was faked
They explain why consultation is unnecessary
questions.explanation: Invited changes may be integral to how the project was conceived.

questions.prompt: How does the conservator view the newest layer?
options: Its age alone does not decide whether to keep it
It must be removed before documentation
It should always be kept
It is valuable only if it matches the first day
questions.explanation: The conservator explicitly rejects newness as a decisive test.

options: A repainting guaranteed to match the first day
Proof that later marks were unauthorised
A decision about which layer should be removed
A view of the earlier state without physically undoing the current one
questions.explanation: A digital version can coexist with the present surface.

questions.prompt: How does the organiser ultimately use the photo?
options: As proof the current surface has no value
As a new mural design
As documentary evidence instead of a conservation instruction
As an image too unreliable to cite
questions.explanation: The concluding turn distinguishes recording a state from ordering a treatment.
